findings.passage: Zada does tune things out, as he did with Harrelson on set, but his accounts of nerves resolving more often describe structure arranged in advance than pressure muted.
findings.problem: The comparative is not supported, including by the edit's own tally. C171 lists three tuning-out remedies against two structure items. The tune-outs are C63, "For my nerves and for me to really attack it, I had to not think about that at all" (S01), the only remedy he explicitly ties to his nerves; C70, "I try to block it all out and stay in my own lane" (S04); and C128, the girlfriend who "helped me relax and not think about work so much" (S30). The structure items are C14, Berlin "prep mode" (S02), and C135, the intimacy-coordinator rehearsals (S20), which the article itself calls standard practice. Counting C136 ("once I felt confident in that", S20) for structure makes it a tie at best. FAQ 2 repeats the claim ("he more often names preparation arranged in advance than pressure tuned out"). This is one of the two Six-over-Nine discriminators, so the overstatement props up the type answer against the main alternative.
findings.acceptance_test: C171 records a stated coding rule and a count of every remedy statement in the record, including S19's "meet all the people I [will be] working with" and C136. The Nine-section sentence and FAQ 2 say only what that count supports, e.g. "about as often". If structure arranged in advance does not clearly outnumber tuning out, the article says the Six-over-Nine case rests on the opposite-of-Woody choice and the preparation habit, and the confidence wording in the type answer, FAQ 1 and the limit paragraph is revisited.

findings.passage: The Six case rests on what settles them: people he knows and preparation done in advance.
findings.problem: On the current record, Six does not beat either alternative on a specific, non-routine discriminator, so a medium-confidence type answer outruns its support. Fear content leans Three (C173, conceded). By the body's own concession, "people he knows" and familiarity are shared with Nine ("'Meet everyone' is about familiarity and ease, which a Nine would also seek"). One of the two structure items is production-run intimacy rehearsal. That leaves one self-described prep-for-nerves statement (S02, July 2025) against an explicit "for my nerves" tune-out (S01), per verify-01. The "rarely a result" test against Three is confounded by timing: most remedy statements predate any release that could have supplied a result, and the one post-result statement (S20) is result-shaped. The article concedes no costly choice favors Six. The record's own alternatives (C50, C165) say that if the structure items are routine, nothing Six-specific remains. Every factual claim I checked holds. The shortfall is a 20-month, almost entirely promotional source base.
findings.acceptance_test: The evidence record adds at least one dated, opened, non-routine discriminator. Acceptable kinds: named third-party or non-promotional testimony on how he handles pressure; a costly choice where he picked trusted people or advance structure over visibility and results (Three) or over the easy path (Nine); or November 2026 press-cycle statements coded against C82/C183. Otherwise confidence is recorded as low and the evidence stays insufficient_evidence. Any confidence or thesis change after the frozen jury goes through --refresh --expanded-review.

findings.passage: so the Six case rests on what settles them: people he knows, a familiar set and preparation done in advance.
findings.problem: FAQ 1, the most widely surfaced answer, lists "a familiar set" (and the type answer lists "people he knows") as the Six case. The body treats familiarity and ease as shared with Nine and therefore non-discriminating.
findings.acceptance_test: The type answer and FAQ 1 name only the remedy items the body counts for Six (structure arranged in advance; Close's "always there for me"), or say in the same sentence that familiarity is shared with Nine.
